object_description: two-storey volume turned 90 degrees from the existing hall, a base with a transparent structure above
geometry_property: turned 90 degrees from the existing hall
clear vertical division into base and attached structure
design_condition: aligning the new building with the existing hall and the eastern plot boundary frees three areas for parking to the north and west and an open sports and lounge area to the south

positive: The alignment frees up three areas for use around the building
A convincingly harmonious ensemble is created across the central square with skilfully placed tree islands
The height of the two-storey building is appropriately integrated into the existing structure
The distances from the building to the neighbouring buildings are generous
A spacious break area is planned as the heart of the facility with varied seating and shady tree islands
An area for two beach volleyball courts adjoins, aligned with the sports part
A multi-use sports area is planned to the north of the existing hall
The two squares are connected by three groups of trees
Bicycle and accessible parking spaces are well and centrally located near the break area
The precise setting takes the existing development into account
The building is clearly divided into a base area and a very transparent attached structure
The sports use in the base and the art use above are clearly visible
The regular column and beam grid results in a calm overall appearance
Water-permeable inlets in the paving are positive for stay quality, microclimate and infiltration
Extensive natural areas with moist hollows, dry locations and native hedges are accommodated
The description shows a high level of expertise and willingness to design close to nature
The main access is aligned towards the existing hall and the main school building
The base area deliberately opens towards the multiple-use outdoor areas
Access is via a spacious covered outdoor area into the foyer
The art floor is organised into three zones divided by floor-to-ceiling trusses
A centrally located, naturally lit open studio and exhibition hall can be used flexibly
It is surrounded by covered outdoor space on two sides
The proposed material meets the client requirements
The economic efficiency indicators are good compared to all projects
The design impresses with simple, coherent organisation and a well-proportioned overall appearance
It accommodates the uses in a compact structure arranged in an optimal operational manner
The outdoor spaces have design quality, high quality of stay and diverse usability
negative: The playground and playing fields on the southern border are likely to cause noise emissions
The running track and volley court marked on the hard surface are unrealistic for sports reasons
The proposed development from one street is not desirable from a traffic planning perspective
Access via the other street is feasible but difficult in clarity and security
Most parking spaces are too small and some are very difficult to use
The exhibition room is more reminiscent of a shop window and is not practical operationally
The routing and vertical access appear somewhat random and purely functional
The art floor is accessed via the two side stairwells, which hides its spatial potential
The complete glazing of the upper floor facade is critical ecologically
Some of the structural dimensions are a bit too slim
The chosen location and formulation of route and vertical access are not very convincing
The development of the parking spaces on the north side is not convincing
